## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

This one-fascicle text by [實叉難陀](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AF%A6%E5%8F%89%E9%9B%A3%E9%99%80) Śikṣānanda is a short Mahāyāna sūtra in which the principal speaker is Samantabhadra (rather than the Buddha himself). The text belongs to the broader *Avataṃsaka*-family of materials that present Samantabhadra as the chief expositor of the cosmic-bodhisattva doctrine, paralleling but not directly corresponding to specific chapters of the *[80-fascicle Huáyán](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0010)* which Śikṣānanda also translated.

The opening reads: "Thus have I heard. At one time the Buddha was at the place sustained by the Tathāgata's spiritual power, together with bodhisattva-mahāsattvas equal in number to the dust-grains of ten unspeakable hundred-thousand-koṭi-nayuta Buddha-fields, who surrounded him front and back, and to whom he expounded the Dharma; all had…"

**Abstract**

The translation belongs to [實叉難陀](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AF%A6%E5%8F%89%E9%9B%A3%E9%99%80) Śikṣānanda's mature period of Cháng'ān translation activity, c. 695 – 710 CE. The bracket adopted here reflects this window. The text is one of several short *Avataṃsaka*-family sūtras Śikṣānanda translated alongside the great *[80-fascicle Huáyán](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0010)*, including *[Dà fāngguǎng rúlái bù sī yì jìngjiè jīng 大方廣如來不思議境界經](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0050)* (T0301).

The text is part of the wider Mahāyāna corpus of "Samantabhadra-sūtras" — sūtras in which Samantabhadra is the principal speaker and which collectively elaborate the *Avataṃsaka*'s programmatic vision of the bodhisattva path under the patronage of Samantabhadra. In the East Asian Buddhist tradition the Samantabhadra-cycle, as crystallised in the *Pǔ-xián xíng-yuàn pǐn* of the *[40-fascicle Avataṃsaka](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0041)* and [不空](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%B8%8D%E7%A9%BA) Amoghavajra's verse-eulogy ([KR6e0046](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0046)), is one of the most influential bodies of devotional literature.

The Taishō text (T0298) is established on the standard apparatus.
